Our Little Bakery

Hi — we're Sweet Layers.

We're a small-batch cake studio in Springfield, founded in 2015 out of a borrowed church kitchen and one very patient oven. Ten years later we still bake the same way Chioma did on day one: real butter, scraped vanilla beans, and zero shortcuts.

— Chioma & the Sweet Layers crew

Est. 2015

How It Started

One oven, a borrowed kitchen, and Grandma Ify's notebook

In the spring of 2015, Chioma baked her first paid cake — lemon blueberry, for a coworker who insisted on paying “real money.” She used her grandmother Ify's handwritten sponge recipe, a borrowed church kitchen after Sunday service, and every mixing bowl she owned. That Saturday, her little farmers-market stall sold out by 10 a.m., and a business accidentally began.

The way we bake hasn't changed much since. Butter, never margarine. Vanilla beans, scraped by hand. Layers baked the morning they're collected — never frozen, never waiting under a fluorescent display case. If a recipe wouldn't pass Grandma Ify's taste test, it doesn't leave our kitchen.

“People forget the napkins. Nobody forgets the cake.”

— Ify, circa forever

Big bakeries will happily sell you a cake off the shelf. We start with a conversation instead — your grandmother's lemon curd, the song that played during the proposal, the exact blush of the bridesmaids' dresses. Those details become the brief, and the brief becomes buttercream.

Because dessert isn't the end of the party. It's the moment everyone leans in. We just make sure it's worth leaning in for.

What We Believe

Four things we'll never compromise

Handcrafted with Care

Every sponge is mixed, baked, and frosted by human hands — no boxed mixes, no shortcuts we wouldn't serve our own families.

Locally Sourced

Eggs, dairy, and seasonal fruit come from farms within an hour of Springfield. Fresher inputs make a better crumb.

Made to Celebrate You

No catalogue cakes here. Every design starts with your story and ends as something nobody else on earth owns.

Every Detail Matters

Level tiers, tempered chocolate, hand-piped borders — the details you notice, and especially the ones you don't.

Behind the Scenes

Life in the sugar studio

Six a.m. flour clouds, radio sing-alongs, and the happiest mess you'll ever see.
